batch: NMR-31/32/33: isolate Native startup from legacy Telegram state while preserving retained data and original-reader rollback compatibility
preparation_state: Implementation/tests authored and independently statically reviewed; new containing-commit Actions execution is pending at receipt creation. This is not acceptance evidence for a future run.
production_change: FabushiAuthService emits only the seven Native v1 credential fields. It no longer reads, creates, rotates, deletes or exports retained Telegram storage/application secrets.

All AppHost constructors converge on the existing constructor, which no longer opens/migrates a Telegram database or creates a TelegramClientLease. HostCreateConfig receives no Telegram client/self identity; old auth calls cannot lazily recreate it.

Existing Native Session/Transcript and native HTTP Human message wiring remains. Existing account/Agent roster and ProductSettings owners remain; legacy proxy publication is unavailable without the client and native-service proxy is not implemented by this batch.
No user-data deletion, schema migration, imported history or replacement owner. Historical FFI/default dependencies remain separately recorded.

state_and_storage.owner: TelegramClientLease owns numeric process registry client. RuntimeClient owns TelegramEngine, AuthorizationMachine, SQLite storage revision, SessionOwner/auth context. Provider from_client_id is non-owning.
state_and_storage.separate_state: TelegramState/telegram:chat:* message identity and encrypted SQLite are independent of native Fabushi Message/Conversation state; runtime additionally tracks operation/turn completion. Adapter output is not evidence of single native message authority.

state_and_storage.migration: Opening store upgrades versions 0/1/2/3 to 4 and rejects >4. Opening is not read-only.
state_and_storage.transaction: Core command uses cloned next state, optimistic expected revision, one SQLite event+snapshot transaction; assigns live core only after commit.
state_and_storage.restart: Loads snapshot/auth/transport and validates Ready requires self identity and transport; challenges require resumable context+transport. SessionOwner and update_state start empty. Provider local negative message counter restarts at -1.

risks.detail: Legacy directory creation, key/decrypt/schema/auth/proxy errors propagate out of AppHost constructor; corrupted old DB can stop normal Fabushi host startup.

AppHost feature.auth.logout forwards FeatureHost logout; does not clear telegram_client. Telegram provider inherits no-op reset_session/set_history_path. Startup lease remains associated with old native account.

AppHost declaration order attempts provider-before-lease drop, but FeatureEventSource owns Arc<FeatureHostController> and can outlive AppHost. Provider numeric id carries no owning lease; stale client lookup fails after lease close.

Provider interrupt returns Ok without changing pending message. Lease close removes registry and SessionOwner Drop cancels owned requests; does not logout remotely or delete DB/key. Authentication-code cancel calls remote cancel and clears context only after success.

Every Provider constructor resets AtomicI64 to -1 while old queue/message IDs persist. QueueMessage rejects an existing chat/local-id tuple; repeated send after restart can collide. No dynamic verification performed.

apply_authorization_state mutates in-memory authorization/self id before save_private_metadata; storage failure does not restore previous in-memory state. Auth and transport are saved in separate metadata operations.
Provider marks queued message completed in runtime event path without network acknowledgment. Do not equate this with actual Telegram send or native Fabushi message integration.

Host/AppHost unconditionally depend on mahayana-telegram; FFI unconditionally depends on fabushi-telegram-runtime and anchors exports. Default isolation does not remove compiled legacy dependency graph.

public_absence_oracle.provider_list: No current AppHost public provider registry list. feature.info exposes only runtimeVersion/protocolVersion/platform; feature.auth.providers returns OAuth providers. Runtime Ready is discarded by FeatureHost translator.
public_absence_oracle.precondition: AppHostFeatureMode::Production and a valid authenticated Fabushi NativeCredential fixture
public_absence_oracle.expected: Synchronous HostResponse.ok=false; full expected error is 'host operation failed: provider is unavailable: telegram'. No feature-event wait is needed.
public_absence_oracle.rationale: ProviderRegistry routing returns that distinct error only when key telegram is absent; a registered unready provider fails later with provider-failed authorization/client error.
